content: Now that I study how measure theory is done in Mathlib, I find the code less readable than math written on paper. Is it a universal experience with measure theory in Mathlib? For most other areas of math, I found the Lean code more readable than what people write on paper.
Can you give examples? Your remark is very vague.
I was intentionally vague because it was my general experience throughout the measure theory in Mathlib.

One example is working with docs#MeasureTheory.MemLp .
Perhaps the source of my discomfort is that "p" is always a part of the name even when it doesn't refer to "p".
For example, on paper people write LqL^qLq so it is immediately clear that only qqq is referenced but writing MemLp _ q somehow still contains the letter "p", which I find mildly confusing.
To be clear, I'm not saying that Mathlib does the notation wrong! I am only asking whether other people have the same experience.
I've never been asking "is it more readable than on paper" with your extreme rigour.
(You could probably write a custom delaborator that replaces MemLp _ q by 𝓛 q, or somesuch.)
Or add an alias MemLebesgue for MemLp and delaborate. Locally, all of these are fixable.
If you're reading code in VS Code (as opposed to insisting printing Lean code on paper or similar).
